div.head: Prom. Reg. 1.3
div.ab: þridde, þæt ic beháte ⁊ bebeode on eallum dómum riht ⁊ mildheortnisse, þæt us eallum arfæst ⁊ mildheort God þurh þæt his ecean miltse forgife, se lifað ⁊ rixað’.
Tertium, ut in omnibus iudiciis aequitatem et misericordiam praecipiam, ut [per hoc] nobis (mihi et uobis) indulgeat suam misericordiam clemens et misericors Deus, qui uiuit [et regnat].
þridde, þæt ic beháte ⁊ bebeode on eallum dómum riht ⁊ mildheortnisse, þæt us eallum arfæst ⁊ mildheort God þurh þæt his ecean miltse forgife, se lifað ⁊ rixað. Finit.

Thirdly, I promise and enjoin justice and mercy in the decision of all cases, in order that God, who liveth and reigneth, may in his grace and mercy be brought thereby to grant us all his eternal compassion.

drittens, dass ich verheisse und gebiete in allen Urtheilssprüchen Recht und Barmherzigkeit, auf dass uns allen deshalb der gnädige und barmherzige Gott seine ewige Gnade schenke, der da lebt und herrscht’.
third, that I promise and command justice and mercy in all judgments, so that the gracious and merciful God, who lives and reigns, may therefore grant us all his eternal mercy’.
div.note: Column O: Latin of the coronation liturgy. Liebermann notes ‘on ecnisse. Amen’ is to be understood after ‘rixað’.
